related_questions.question: How close is type 1 diabetes to being cured?
related_questions.snippet: The only known cure for Type 1 diabetes is either a pancreas transplant or a transplant of the specialized pancreatic cells that produce insulin. But with a shortage of available organs and 1.6 million people in the U.S. living with the disease, a cure for the vast majority is not possible.

related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of someone with type 1 diabetes?

text_blocks.snippet: The average life expectancy for someone with type 1 diabetes is generally lower than for someone without the condition, but advancements in treatment have significantly improved survival rates over time. Studies show that people with type 1 diabetes may live about 10-12 years less than those without diabetes. However, this gap is narrowing due to better management of the condition.
snippet_highlighted_words: 10-12 years less than those without diabetes

list.title: Historically:
list.snippet: Before the discovery of insulin, type 1 diabetes was often fatal, with most people dying within a few years of diagnosis.

list.title: Current estimates:
list.snippet: A 20-year-old diagnosed with type 1 diabetes can expect to live about 10-12 years less than their non-diabetic peers.
Age at diagnosis: Earlier diagnosis generally correlates with a shorter lifespan.
Blood sugar control: Better blood glucose management is associated with longer survival.
Access to healthcare and resources: Availability of insulin, monitoring tools, and comprehensive care play a crucial role.
Other health conditions: The presence of complications like diabetic nephropathy or cardiovascular disease can also impact lifespan.

list.title: Improvements in treatment:
list.snippet: Modern treatments like insulin therapy, continuous glucose monitoring, and advancements in managing complications have dramatically improved life expectancy compared to the past.

list.title: Example:
list.snippet: Studies from Finland show that a 20-year-old with type 1 diabetes in 2017 had a life expectancy about 10 years lower than the general population, according to research.
